title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #7

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why do farmers remove weeds from a crop field? (1 mark)
   A. To make weeds grow
   B. To stop rain falling
   C. To harm the crops
   D. So crops get enough water, light and space

2. Which part of the plant holds it firmly in the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Flowers
   B. Leaves
   C. Fruit
   D. Roots

3. What can you use to draw and label a plant if you have a computer at school? (1 mark)
   A. A calculator only
   B. A drawing app
   C. A stopwatch
   D. A ruler only

4. Which of these is a stem that stores food and is eaten or used for sugar? (1 mark)
   A. Sukuma wiki leaf
   B. Sugarcane
   C. Tomato
   D. Bean pod

5. Which of these is a safety rule when handling plants? (1 mark)
   A. Ask an adult before touching a plant you do not know
   B. Pull plants with thorns barehanded
   C. Taste every fruit you find
   D. Rub sap on your eyes

6. Which group of vertebrates feeds its young on milk? (1 mark)
   A. Birds
   B. Mammals
   C. Fish
   D. Reptiles

7. A bat flies but has fur and feeds its babies milk. What is it? (1 mark)
   A. A bird
   B. A mammal
   C. An insect
   D. A reptile

8. Which of these animals gives birth to live young? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Housefly
   C. Goat
   D. Frog

9. Which of these is a safe thing to do on a science walk? (1 mark)
   A. Throw stones at birds
   B. Wash your hands after touching soil or animals
   C. Tease insects
   D. Pick up unknown snakes

10. In the mouth, which part helps to move food around and swallow? (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Tongue
   C. Gullet
   D. Stomach

11. Why is it important to eat slowly? (1 mark)
   A. It stops you growing
   B. It lets you chew well and helps digestion
   C. It makes food taste of salt
   D. It makes you thirsty

12. Which of these is true of a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. It has no volume
   B. It has a fixed volume but no fixed shape
   C. It fills a room
   D. It has a fixed shape but no fixed volume

13. Which of these is a solid? (1 mark)
   A. Milk
   B. Air
   C. Steam
   D. A stone

14. Why are liquids useful for drinking? (1 mark)
   A. They cannot flow
   B. They keep their own shape
   C. They are always hot
   D. They can be poured and swallowed

15. Why are gumboots useful when handling waste? (1 mark)
   A. They make waste rot
   B. They make hands clean
   C. They make waste lighter
   D. They protect the feet from sharp things and dirt

16. Which of these is NOT a way of managing solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Composting
   B. Throwing it in a river
   C. Recycling
   D. Reusing

17. What is a good use of old clothes? (1 mark)
   A. Bury them in a garden pit
   B. Use them as cleaning cloths
   C. Burn them near a house
   D. Throw them in a drain

18. Which of these is a reason to conserve water? (1 mark)
   A. To make taps rust
   B. To waste less time
   C. To make it more expensive
   D. There will be enough for everyone

19. Why should a rainwater tank be covered? (1 mark)
   A. To make water heavier
   B. To keep out mosquitoes and dirt
   C. To make it rain
   D. To keep the water warm

20. Which of these is a use of friction? (1 mark)
   A. Machines wearing out
   B. Wasting energy
   C. Brakes stopping a bicycle
   D. Making parts hot

21. Which of these is a way of increasing useful friction? (1 mark)
   A. Shoes with rough soles
   B. Polishing a table
   C. Wearing smooth socks on a wet floor
   D. Oiling a floor

22. What effect does friction have on rubbing your hands? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them cold
   B. It makes them heavy
   C. It makes them wet
   D. It makes them warm

23. Which surface gives the most friction? (1 mark)
   A. An oiled floor
   B. A smooth ice surface
   C. A rough carpet
   D. A polished tile

24. A rolling ball slowly comes to a stop on the ground mainly because of (1 mark)
   A. Sound
   B. Light
   C. Colour
   D. Friction

25. Which of these will make a block slide the shortest distance on a ramp? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Oiled plastic
   C. Smooth tile
   D. Sandpaper

26. Which of these is a safe practice with light? (1 mark)
   A. Shine torches in eyes
   B. Look at the sun with your eyes
   C. Never look straight at the sun
   D. Stare at bright lights

27. What does a translucent roof sheet do? (1 mark)
   A. Creates sound
   B. Blocks all light
   C. Lets some light in
   D. Makes light

28. How can lights help protect a home? (1 mark)
   A. Lights make walls hot
   B. Lights make people sleep
   C. Security lights help keep thieves away
   D. Lights make doors open

29. Why are pot handles often made of wood or plastic? (1 mark)
   A. They get very hot
   B. They are heavy
   C. They pass heat quickly
   D. They pass heat slowly

30. Why is a thermometer better than touching to find how hot something is? (1 mark)
   A. It is heavy
   B. It is dangerous
   C. It is safe and gives a number
   D. It is noisy

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Why should you not touch a hot object to find out how hot it is? What should you use? (3 marks)

32. Explain how a frog is similar to and different from a fish. (4 marks)

33. Explain why steam from a kettle is invisible although we see a white cloud above the spout. Say what state of matter the cloud is. (5 marks)

34. Explain why rubbing your hands makes them warm. (2 marks)

35. Describe the journey of a mouthful of food from the mouth to the anus. (4 marks)

36. Give three ways of lighting a house at night. (3 marks)

37. Describe how to make a pair of kitchen gloves from local materials. (4 marks)

38. A pupil pulls up a small bean plant from the garden. Describe what she will see and give the job of each part she sees. (5 marks)

39. Explain why cooking pots are made of metal but their handles are not. (4 marks)

40. Discuss how a family can light their home cheaply and safely. (5 marks)

41. Give four ways in which heat is used in farming. (4 marks)

42. Describe how to show that metal passes heat more easily than wood. (3 marks)

43. What is the difference between a vertebrate and an invertebrate? (2 marks)

44. Give two ways of reducing waste at home. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — So crops get enough water, light and space
   Weeds compete with crops for water, light and room.

2. D — Roots
   Roots anchor the plant in the ground.

3. B — A drawing app
   A drawing app can be used to draw and label plant parts.

4. B — Sugarcane
   Sugarcane stems store sugar.

5. A — Ask an adult before touching a plant you do not know
   Some plants can hurt or poison people, so ask first.

6. B — Mammals
   Mammals feed their babies with milk.

7. B — A mammal
   The fur and milk feeding make it a mammal.

8. C — Goat
   Goats are mammals and give birth to live young. Hens, frogs and flies lay eggs.

9. B — Wash your hands after touching soil or animals
   Handling animals safely and washing hands avoids injury and germs.

10. B — Tongue
   The tongue moves food and helps swallowing.

11. B — It lets you chew well and helps digestion
   Chewing well breaks food down before swallowing.

12. B — It has a fixed volume but no fixed shape
   A liquid has a fixed volume and takes the container's shape.

13. D — A stone
   A stone keeps its shape.

14. D — They can be poured and swallowed
   Liquids pour easily.

15. D — They protect the feet from sharp things and dirt
   Boots protect feet from cuts and germs.

16. B — Throwing it in a river
   Throwing waste in rivers pollutes water.

17. B — Use them as cleaning cloths
   Reusing old cloth as cleaning cloths reduces waste.

18. D — There will be enough for everyone
   Conserving leaves water for others.

19. B — To keep out mosquitoes and dirt
   A cover stops mosquitoes breeding and dirt getting in.

20. C — Brakes stopping a bicycle
   Brakes use friction to slow wheels.

21. A — Shoes with rough soles
   Rough soles grip the ground.

22. D — It makes them warm
   Friction produces heat.

23. C — A rough carpet
   Rough surfaces give more friction.

24. D — Friction
   Friction between the ball and the ground slows it.

25. D — Sandpaper
   Rough surfaces have the most friction.

26. C — Never look straight at the sun
   Looking at the sun harms eyes.

27. C — Lets some light in
   It lets daylight in but you cannot see through it clearly.

28. C — Security lights help keep thieves away
   Thieves avoid places where they can be seen.

29. D — They pass heat slowly
   Handles stay cooler.

30. C — It is safe and gives a number
   A thermometer avoids burns and measures.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can burn your skin. Use a thermometer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for burns, 1 mark for using a thermometer, 1 mark for reason it is safe.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Both are vertebrates and have a backbone. A frog has moist skin and lives on land and in water, and a fish lives in water and has gills and fins.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for similarity and 2 marks for differences.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Steam is water as a gas and it is invisible. The white cloud is made of tiny water drops which are liquid.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for steam is a gas, 1 mark for invisible, 1 mark for white cloud being tiny drops, 1 mark for liquid, 1 mark for a clear explanation.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Rubbing causes friction and friction produces heat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for friction and 1 mark for heat.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Chewed in the mouth, swallowed, pushed down the gullet, churned in the stomach, digested and absorbed in the small intestine, water taken back in the large intestine, faeces stored in the rectum and passed out of the anus.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for every two correct steps up to 4.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Electric bulbs, solar lamps, paraffin lamps, candles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose thick cotton cloth or old towel. Trace and cut two mitten shapes. Add an inner layer. Sew them together leaving the wrist open. Turn it inside out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: She will see roots that hold the plant and take in water, a stem that holds it up and carries food and water, leaves that make food, and maybe flowers or pods that make seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming each of four parts and 1 mark for correct function overall.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Metal passes heat quickly to the food so it cooks. Handles made of wood or plastic pass heat slowly so our hands do not burn.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the pot and 2 marks for the handle.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: Use windows and translucent sheets by day, solar lamps and LED bulbs at night, keep candles and paraffin away from cloth, turn off lights when not needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drying grain and crops, hatching chicks, keeping chicks warm, cooking, controlling pests, drying fish.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put a metal spoon and a wooden spoon into a cup of warm water. After two minutes touch the top of each. The metal feels warmer so metal passes heat easily.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: A vertebrate has a backbone and an invertebrate has no backbone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Buy less packaging, carry a reusable bag, cook only what is needed, repair things.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
